Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites. For bosonic atoms, we further show how the tautochrone dynamics is shaped by lattice inhomogeneity, phase-space structure, and on-site interactions.

title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
summary: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
comment: 26 pages, 17 figures, 8 tables. Corrects the analysis of E. O. Silva, Opt. Quantum Electron. 58, 113 (2026), doi:10.1007/s11082-026-08693-8, whose retraction has been requested. Scripts and verification tests are provided as ancillary files
summary: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.
